app.h2: The screens your team will use every day.
app.n00p: Every chat is listed by its first question, grouped by day. Nothing replaces the chat you have open.
app.n01p: Open a second chat and tabs appear. Drag to reorder, close when you are done.
app.n02p: Every answer has a summary, a chart, the row count and the time. Change the view with one click.
app.n10p: Requests that touch an ask-first table wait here, with the person, their role and the exact question.
app.n11: See the SQL before it runs
app.n11p: The query is shown in full, with each table it reads.
app.n12p: Approval runs that one query, and the person who asked gets a notification.
app.n20p: Analysts and Viewers see each table as allowed, ask first or blocked. You set it once.
app.n21p: Hidden tables are left out of the schema your AI provider sees.
app.n22p: The rules are checked in code on every query. A model cannot talk its way past them.
app.n30p: Status, versions and when it was last seen, read live from your server.
app.n31p: Database, cache and both AI models are checked one by one, each with its own result.
app.n32p: You see counts per day for 7, 30 or 90 days. The questions themselves stay on your server.
app.n40p: Admins confirm every sign-in with a 6-digit code. Other users can turn it on.
app.n41p: A code works once and expires after 10 minutes.
app.n42p: Too many wrong codes lock the attempt. Your admin helps you back in.
app.n50: The whole product, not a viewer
app.n50p: Ask, change views and read history on a phone, down to 360 px wide.
app.n51p: The sidebar slides in from the left and closes when you pick a chat.
app.n52p: Wide admin tables turn into cards, so nothing needs a sideways scroll.
app.p: One window for questions, a quiet inbox for approvals, and settings an admin can read at a glance. It works the same way on a phone.

faq.a0: Your database, the queries, the results, the chat history and the audit log all stay on the Appliance on your server. Central only handles sign-in, organisation settings and routing. It stores no questions, SQL or results.
faq.a1: The question from the browser and the answer going back pass through Central and an encrypted tunnel. Central doesn't store or log them. Each request carries a signed identity token that the Appliance verifies.
faq.a10: PostgreSQL and Microsoft SQL Server. You can ask in English, Turkish or German.
faq.a11: “Lock-in.” It comes from the Latin loqui, “to speak”. Say what you want to know, and lock in on the answer.
faq.a2: Not by default. Queries run through a read-only user. If your policy allows changes, they only happen after a preview and a confirmation. Schema commands never run.
faq.a3: To write the SQL: your question, the schema and the last few turns of the conversation. No table rows. You choose the provider and the keys.
faq.a4: It never runs. The blocked SQL and the reason go into the audit log on your server.
faq.a5: The schema is scanned during setup. An admin marks each table as allowed, approval-only or blocked for Analysts and Viewers, and can change it at any time.
faq.a6: Either. We install Loquein on your own server or in your own cloud account. Either way, the Appliance runs under your control.
faq.a7: We install together with you, using temporary access you grant for the setup only. It's removed when we're done.
faq.a8: As signed releases. You decide when to install them, and a release whose signature doesn't check out won't install.
faq.a9: You set the retention period for chat and audit logs. They stay on your server, and backups are encrypted.

hero.kicker: AI for your database · on your own server
hero.lead: Your data stays locked in on your own server. Your team is free to ask it anything, in plain words. No SQL, no report queue.
ins.h2: Installed without opening a door. Server ready? 1–3 working days.
ins.p0: Your own machine or your cloud account. Linux, Docker, outbound HTTPS and a few standard tools.
ins.p1: The package lands on your server and its signature is checked. No match, no install.
ins.p2: The Appliance starts as a handful of Docker services and runs its own health checks.
ins.p3: Your server makes the call: an encrypted tunnel out to Central. Not a single inbound port.
ins.p4: It connects with a read-only user and scans the schema. You decide which role sees which table.
ins.p5: Invite your team. Updates arrive as signed releases, on your schedule.
meta.desc: Loquein lets your team ask your database questions in plain words. It runs on your own server, checks every query against your rules and sends no table rows to the AI.
meta.title: Loquein — The good kind of lock-in.
price.p: We look at seats, databases and how you deploy, then send a tailored quote after a short call.
prod.aiP: Your provider, your key. The call leaves from your own server.
prod.b1a: Each answer carries a short summary, the result table and, where it fits, a chart.
prod.b1b: Roles with permission also see the SQL that ran. Timing and row count are on every answer.
prod.b1c: Export the result and drop it into your report.
prod.b2H: The conversation picks up where it left off.
prod.b2a: “And last month?” is enough. The previous question and its query are remembered.
prod.b2b: Only the recent turns go to the model. Result rows never do.
prod.b2c: Every follow-up goes through your rules again.
prod.b3H: Same result, the shape you want.
prod.b3a: The right view is picked from the shape of the result.
prod.b3b: Change it with a sentence like “make it a line chart”, or with one click.
prod.b3c: Switching views never re-runs the query. Your database is not touched again.
prod.b4H: Sensitive data waits for a yes.
prod.b4a: A question that touches an approval-only table doesn't run. It lands in the admin's inbox.
prod.b4b: The admin sees who asked, the question and the SQL, then allows it once or declines.
prod.b4c: Until then, not a single row is read.
prod.b5H: Code enforces the rule, not the model.
prod.b5a: Analysts and Viewers each have three lists: allowed, needs approval, closed.
prod.b5b: Every query is parsed and checked against these lists before it runs.
prod.b5c: A query for a closed table never runs. Talking the model into it doesn't help.
prod.b6H: The key stays on your server.
prod.b6a: The provider key is stored encrypted on your server. No screen ever shows it again.
prod.b6b: What the model gets: the question, the schema and the recent turns. What it never gets: table rows.
prod.b6c: Only model profiles that passed our tests can be selected.
prod.b7H: Read-only by default, and it can stay that way.
prod.b7a: Only you turn writes on, role by role and table by table.
prod.b7b: Every change is previewed before it runs and waits for your confirmation.
prod.b7c: Schema commands such as dropping a table are closed to everyone, admins included.
prod.fP: No need to start over. Loquein remembers where the conversation left off.
prod.gH: Sensitive tables wait for a yes.
prod.gP: Questions that touch them go to an admin first, who sees the SQL and who asked.

story.h2: One question, six stops. Your database stays put.
story.p0: Someone on your team types a question. It leaves the browser over HTTPS, headed for Central.
story.p1: Central keeps nothing. It passes the request, with a signed identity token, through an encrypted tunnel to the Appliance on your server.
story.p2: The Appliance sends your AI provider the question, the schema and the last few turns. Never table rows.
story.p3: Before anything runs, the SQL is parsed. Every table and operation it touches is checked against your role's policy.
story.p4: The query runs on your server through a read-only database user. Your database doesn't move an inch.
story.p5: The answer travels back the same encrypted way, only to the person who asked. No copy is left along the route.
